prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one coherent scene and moment, no panels or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: A Show for Two; World Discovery; fiction.
Setting: World Discovery classroom play table on a bright afternoon; Kit and Zoe wear their locked everyday outfits.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): A stage made from six chunky tan blocks; One white paper scene with two green trees; One rectangular card with Kit’s simple stick-legged dog drawing; One dog-shaped paper puppet with floppy brown ears, attached to one wide craft stick; its red collar is added on page six; One red crayon; One plain gray drawing pencil for Kit’s first dog sketch
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and development stage required below.
Page 4. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): Kit studies her folded paper. “It needs something stiff behind it.”
Required illustration: World Discovery classroom play table on a bright afternoon; Kit and Zoe wear their locked everyday outfits. Kit holds the limp scenery paper upright with one hand and looks at his block stage behind it. Exact state: Paper only held, not yet supported; blocks remain assembled.
Exact current state: Paper only held, not yet supported; blocks remain assembled.
Do not add later events, duplicate props or a separate inset. No written title; the app renders live text.
Critical exact-state composition: Kit holds the ONE flexible two-tree scenery sheet upright with ONE hand; the sheet is still limp and not yet propped on the blocks. The six-block stage stands behind the paper, with a visible gap so it is not touching/supporting the sheet yet. ONE dog puppet without red collar remains lying flat nearby. No duplicate sheets.

visualReview.note: Kit supports the flexible scenery sheet with one hand, visibly separate from the six-block stage; collarless dog puppet lies on table. The paper has not been fixed to blocks yet.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent image/sequence inspection; not physical classroom observation.
